info.title: Socrates Backend API
info.description:
REST + SSE API consumed by the Socrates web SPA and the Expo Android
shell. The existing
endpoints (auth, captcha, sessions, share, api-key, migrate,
chat, agent, search, fetch-batch) are summarised at the end
of this file for completeness; the new endpoints introduced
by the P1-P6 feature enhancements are documented in detail.

JSON writes may send Idempotency-Key (1-200 printable ASCII characters,
excluding spaces). POST /api/projects, /api/prompts, /api/scheduled-tasks,
POST /api/sessions/{sessionId}/archive, PATCH /api/users/me,
PATCH /api/users/me/preferences and PUT /api/sessions/{sessionId}/tags persist
successful JSON responses atomically with their database writes. These operations
support replay across instances and restarts for 24 hours after commit, scoped to
the authenticated user, credential and operation (including the session ID).
Authentication and existing route permissions run before every replay.
Object key order is ignored when comparing bodies; array order matters.
Invalid keys return 400 on these operations. Credential rotation starts a
new scope. The original response is replayed even if the resource changed.

Other JSON writes use a process-local cache for up to 24 hours, subject to
eviction, and do not survive restart. For both mechanisms a concurrent
repeat returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS with Retry-After: 1; changed
bodies return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Responses exceeding 256 KiB retain
a completion marker: retries return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_RESULT_UNAVAILABLE;
retrieve the resource instead of repeating the write. The process-local
cache can also return 503 IDEMPOTENCY_CAPACITY with Retry-After: 1.
Uploads, SSE and external effects need operation-specific guarantees.

post.summary: Atomically create a chat turn and its initial event
post.description:
Concurrent requests with the same (user, clientTurnId) return one
durable turn. This creates a record; it does not itself start an LLM
worker. Use the chat stream's turn binding to execute it. A clientTurnId
cannot be rebound to a different session. The chat stream atomically
claims a queued turn before model/tool work. Repeated execution attempts
emit an SSE error with CONFLICT (the primed HTTP status remains 200).
Reconnect to the event endpoint instead. Heartbeat-expired executions
become interrupted and require an explicit new turn to retry.

201.description: Created, with turn, created=true and capabilities.resumable=true

404.description: Session does not exist or is not owned by the caller

409.description: clientTurnId was already bound to a different session

get.summary: Replay and tail an owned turn's durable events
get.description:
Sends event: turn_event with {turnId, sequence, event, data} JSON,
followed by chat-protocol aliases. Content aliases are default SSE
data events containing delta; reasoning aliases contain reasoning.
Other aliases use their original event name. Resume with after=lastSeq.
Replay drains all available pages; a one-second database poll catches
events written by another server instance. Disconnecting unsubscribes
this reader and does not interrupt the worker. Event persistence does
not by itself imply worker restart recovery.

200.description: Ordered SSE event envelopes and compatibility aliases

get.summary: List the current user's latest 50 research jobs

post.summary: Queue research independently of the browser connection
post.description:
Requires chat:write. At most three queued/running jobs per user.
The required body idempotencyKey is persisted with the job (independent
of the general Idempotency-Key header middleware). Repeating the key
and normalized payload returns the current snapshot of the same job;
changing the payload returns 409. Ownership and session/project
consistency are checked. sessionId and projectId default to null.
Research uses the owner's active server-stored model provider.

404.description: Session or project is not owned by this user

409.description: Key payload mismatch or active job limit exceeded

get.description: Requires chat:read. The resultArtifactId points to a private Markdown artifact retrieved through the existing artifacts API. Provider errors use redacted research_* codes.

Requires chat:read. A successful session-bound job commits its report
message, private Markdown/LaTeX artifacts and terminal event in one transaction. The
message uses a stable clientId of research-{jobId}. This endpoint
returns the current canonical message so reconnecting clients do not
duplicate reports or restore text the user has edited or deleted.
Returns null before success, for a session-less job, or after message
deletion. The artifact remains available independently.

200.description: Canonical saved report message or null

get.description:
Requires chat:read. Persisted events are replayed in sequence order,
then polled across worker processes. Frames contain id (sequence),
event: research_event, and JSON data matching ResearchJobEvent.
Last-Event-ID takes precedence over after. Disconnecting only closes
the subscription; research continues. Slow consumers are disconnected
and should reconnect with their last received ID. The stream closes
after all terminal events; clients should refresh the snapshot before
deciding whether to reconnect. No lease tokens or source bodies leak.

200.description: Ordered lifecycle event stream with keepalives

post.description: Requires chat:write. Revokes the lease immediately. Repeating cancellation of a terminal job returns its current snapshot. In-flight read-only provider work may finish but cannot commit.

Requires chat:write. Requeues a failed/cancelled job, retains valid checkpoints and event sequence, and resets the recovery attempt budget. Empty-source failures repeat search. Only queued or expired-running work is claimed automatically, up to three lease attempts. Provider calls have a ten-minute execution deadline per attempt.

409.description: Job cannot be retried or active job limit exceeded

post.description:
Requires chat:write. Atomically cancels the active source job and
queues a replacement with the same question plus a durable user focus
instruction. The source snapshot is returned as previous so clients
can preserve the task history. The replacement starts with a clean
plan and is subject to the same three-active-job limit.

202.description: Source task cancelled and replacement queued

409.description: Job is not active or the active job limit would be exceeded

200.description: Scheduled tasks owned by the current user

post.description: Database-backed idempotent JSON write; see the Idempotency-Key contract above.

post.summary: Execute a scheduled task immediately without moving its next slot
post.description:
Manual and scheduled executions share a database lease. Completion
commits result messages and bookkeeping together. A busy task returns
409; sequential manual runs are distinct executions. Native LLM tasks
whose worker dies can be reclaimed after lease expiry. Workspace-agent
runs with unknown external effects are paused instead of automatically
replayed; review their run history before manually retrying. Pauses and
reschedules made during provider work are preserved.

409.description: Task already running or expired agent outcome uncertain; uncertain tasks are paused

get.summary: EXISTING — public read-only view
EXISTING — list BYO providers
get.description: Returns the caller's provider rows. Every row carries a `capabilities` summary derived from that model's own contract, so a client never has to infer what the model can do from its name — the built-in provider's model name is deliberately not exposed. The response also carries `builtInCapabilities`: the built-in provider is a system row and is therefore not part of the caller's list, but its capability summary travels beside the list.

200.description: The caller's providers plus the built-in provider's capability summary

post.summary: EXISTING
EXISTING — localStorage → server migration
EXISTING — non-streaming chat
post.description: Returns the canonical `content` field and a temporary OpenAI-compatible `choices[0].message.content` view for older auxiliary clients. Native tool definitions are used only by the streaming endpoint. Requests may set `response_speed` to `standard` or `fast`; unsupported priority service automatically falls back to standard and is reported in meta. An optional `assistantId` selects an owned configurable assistant; an owned `sessionId` restores that session's assistant when omitted. Instant mode is resolved against the model's declared capability: the server encodes it the way that model documents it — `reasoning_effort: none`, `thinking: {type: disabled}`, `enable_thinking: false`, or `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}`. Explicit no-thinking controls are preserved during compatibility retries; a model that cannot switch thinking off is rejected before any upstream call rather than silently resuming thinking. Reasoning-effort levels are translated into the provider's own vocabulary, and are not sent at all to a model that documents no such levels.

post.summary: EXISTING — SSE chat
post.description: The server injects the native tool contract from the exact tool registry for the current turn. Tool arguments are one JSON object that matches the supplied function schema, without an input or arguments wrapper. The stream shares the authenticated chat rate-limit bucket. Instant uses the same provider-specific no-thinking controls as `/api/chat`. A successful priority-service fallback emits `preference_fallback` before content frames. Provider retries share an eight-second automatic backoff budget per upstream call, including compatibility variants. A longer Retry-After is reported without waiting or retrying before the provider cooldown. Named `error` frames retain `status`, `code`, `message`, and `retryable`; provider failures additionally carry optional `upstreamStatus` and `retryAfterMs` (milliseconds, a retry hint rather than guaranteed availability). Exhausted provider retries set `retryable: false` so clients do not replay the whole turn. Older clients may ignore the additional fields. The same fields are used by JSON provider errors. Optional `turn_event` frames provide the version 1 public turn runtime. Every event has `version: 1`, `turnId`, strictly increasing `seq`, `at` (Unix milliseconds), and `type`. Payloads are `activity.upsert` with an `activity` (stable id, kind, phase, startedAt, optional endedAt, public text, toolCallId and toolName), `generation` with phase streaming, `ui.begin` with surfaceId/toolCallId/textOffset, `ui.add` with surfaceId/node, `ui.patch` with surfaceId/nodeId/props, `ui.commit` with surfaceId/nodes, `ui.abort` with surfaceId, or `turn.done` with phase done/failed/stopped and optional durationMs. Additive evidence events are `source.upsert` with source `{id,url,title,snippet}` and `claim.annotate` with claim `{id,start,end,quote,citationIds}` plus citations `[{id,sourceId}]`. Claim offsets are UTF-16 indices into raw assistant text, end-exclusive; quote must match visible prose exactly. Sources originate only from successful web_search/web_fetch results; annotation does not imply independent verification of a claim. The native cite_sources tool binds already-written prose to registered source IDs. Unknown sources, ambiguous quotes, private/code/math spans and overlapping claims reject the complete tool batch. Sources/citations/claims persist in turnRuntime (limits 80/80/128). The SPA renders inline references, source previews and a Sources disclosure; legacy clients may continue showing tool cards. `ui.edit` carries surfaceId, baseRevision and atomic operations `[{op:patch,nodeId,props}|{op:add,node}|{op:remove,nodeId}]`. The native patch_intelligent_ui tool edits committed surfaces in the current live turn only. Revision starts at 0 and increments once per accepted transaction; stale revisions reject all operations. Remove also removes descendants. Full graph, URL, size and safety validation applies; at least one node must remain. Surviving node IDs and local control state are preserved. Activity phases are running/done/failed/stopped; kinds are waiting/reasoning/tool/synthesis/reasoning_summary. Only reasoning_summary entries carry public model-provided text. A generation event does not finish activities or tools. Clients deduplicate by turnId and seq; unknown versions/types may be ignored. UI patches cannot change node identity/type/parent and must pass the full UI validator. UI commit replaces the preview with the validated final document; abort retracts it. Only complete validated nodes stream before tool_use. Incomplete nodes and unresolved parents wait. Tool failure or malformed arguments retract the preview; successful execution commits it. Existing tool_use/tool_result frames and stored toolCalls remain the compatible final representation. The bounded turnRuntime snapshot is saved/restored on session messages. Detached turn event replay includes these same public runtime events. Optional `turn_activity` frames report public observations: `{type: thinking}`, `{type: tool, toolCallId, toolName}`, `{type: synthesizing}`, or `{type: done, durationMs}`. Clients must wait for stream playback to settle before mounting answer actions. Private reasoning is never activity copy. Older clients may ignore this additive event. Optional `turn_summary` frames carry `{summary}` for a completed activity retrospective. Completed summaries use observed execution facts and do not require another model request before the closing frame. Plain answers without reasoning or tools may omit the retrospective. The native `render_intelligent_ui` tool accepts `{version: 1, nodes: [...]}` with 1–80 unique typed nodes. Server validation rejects unsafe keys, URLs, invalid parents and cycles. UI data travels through ordinary tool_use/tool_result frames and stored toolCalls, separate from prose. Existing clients can display a generic tool result; legacy UI fences remain readable on the web for old sessions. Nodes may additionally use `type: openui` with a nonempty `source` string (maximum 50000 characters) containing OpenUI Lang 1.0. The SPA lazily renders the curated declarative library; existing clients may display the generic tool result. Native patch operations can update source. Local OpenUI state survives source extensions on the same node ID. The SPA also recognizes streamed fenced `openui` programs in prose; these fences are removed from copy and speech output like existing socrates-ui fences. Same-origin map and image-search endpoints are supplied under /api/intelligent-ui; no additional provider key, arbitrary Query/Mutation provider or executable HTML is supplied. Shared packages carry only data; the React OpenUI renderer belongs to the SPA until Universal App artifact migration signs off.

get.summary: Resolve real OpenUI SearchImage results with source attribution
get.description: Requires the normal authenticated session. Accepts a 2–200 character query. Searches Wikimedia Commons, then DuckDuckGo image results and the existing Bing provider when earlier sources are unavailable or empty. Returns up to eight raster images with same-origin proxy URLs, title, sourceUrl, and author/license when supplied by Commons. Empty upstream failures return 502 and are not cached as successful results. Search and asset requests are rate limited. The browser never receives a provider API key or an arbitrary proxy.

200.description: Images with URLs under /api/v2/intelligent-ui/image and attribution

get.summary: Serve a supported provider's raster thumbnail through the same origin
get.description: Authenticated, rate limited proxy restricted to HTTPS Wikimedia upload paths and Bing thumbnail hosts. Rejects credentials, custom ports, redirects, SVG/HTML responses, and bodies above five MB. Uses a bounded 32 MiB shared asset cache and sends nosniff. Cookies and credentials are never forwarded upstream. This endpoint cannot fetch arbitrary URLs.

200.description: Raster image with its verified content type

502.description: Upstream image unavailable or unsafe response

get.summary: Resolve a named place using Photon and OpenStreetMap data
get.description: Requires authentication. Returns up to five candidates with label, latitude, longitude and the matching OpenStreetMap source URL. A marker's place field should include landmark, city and country to disambiguate. No autocomplete is performed; the SPA waits for stable model output.

200.description: Place candidates; an empty array means no place was located

get.summary: Fetch a driving route overview between verified coordinates
get.description: Authenticated OSRM request for two to twenty-five stops, encoded as lng,lat;lng,lat. Returns GeoJSON-order points ([longitude,latitude]), distance in meters, duration in seconds and profile driving. This is not walking or turn-by-turn guidance. A failure never substitutes a direct connection for a street route. Successful routes cache ten minutes.

get.summary: Return OpenFreeMap TileJSON with same-origin tile templates
get.description: Authenticated, cached metadata from the fixed OpenFreeMap provider. Accepts only that provider's versioned planet template and rewrites every tile URL to /api/v2/intelligent-ui/maps/tiles. MapLibre and its worker are bundled, and glyphs also use a same-origin endpoint. No CSP host expansion or client key is required.

200.description: TileJSON 3.0 with supported tile URLs and attribution

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Reuse the same key and JSON body to retry a write within 24 hours, using the same credential.

IdempotencyConflict.description: Request still in progress, body conflict, or completed result too large to retain.

Forbidden.description: CSRF missing or wrong, or wrong owner

ProviderCapabilities.description: What a provider's model can actually do, derived from the model's own documented contract. Every field is optional: a client that receives no summary must keep working and must read an absent field as "nothing is known", never as "unsupported".

isReasoning.description: The model reasons — it has a thinking channel of its own.

supportsInstant.description: The user may ask for "no thinking" (Instant).

supportsEffort.description: The model accepts a reasoning-effort level.

accessToken.description: Short-lived bearer credential; send as Authorization Bearer.

refreshToken.description: Rotating opaque credential; only accepted by refresh/logout.

clientId.description: Stable client identity used to deduplicate restored messages
